judgment.notes: Checked all five M applications against their supplied statements and bound signatures. A001 uses M009 at the real endpoints inf B_i,sup B_i, whose existence and ordering are established in S001, and at 0,1; M009 has no additional hypotheses. Empty members use the measure empty-set axiom. A002 uses M011 on the Borel real line with Lebesgue volume, lower function g and upper function the sum of f_seq; F003 supplies the required everywhere inequality, and no measurability premise is imposed. A003 uses M010 with J=ℕ, W=ℝ, μ=volume and f=f_seq; countability is immediate and F003 establishes measurable, hence almost-everywhere measurable, summands. Its conclusion is precisely the exchange in S004, even for infinite sums. A004 and A005 use M012 on I with constant c and on I∩J_i with constant ρ_i^s respectively; F002 gives both measurability premises, and both constants lie in ℝ≥0∞. No finiteness premise is needed. N001 is instantiated at (X,A,s) for the slice covers and at (MaxProd(X),A×I,s+1) for the product infimum and scale supremum; s>0 and s+1>0. The elementary power comparison implicit in the slice cost is justified in BG004. There are no external E inputs.

S001 constructs bounded projections and actual finite endpoints, with interval length at most ρ_i. S003 proves coverage for each fixed t∈I and obtains c≤the slice majorant by N001 and monotonicity of positive powers. The zero branch proves the inequality outside I. S004 integrates this inequality, evaluates the measurable indicators, and bounds the resulting series by the product-cover cost. The computation is valid for c=∞, zero-diameter members and divergent series; no subtraction or division of infinite quantities occurs. S005 uses the lower-infimum property, including the empty collection of admissible covers, then order monotonicity of suprema over δ>0. These operations establish every clause of N003.

scope: Coverage is reviewer-reported; reading alone is not mathematical assessment.
